title: BrushOff: Stroke-Based Re-rendering as a Watermark Removal Attack on Paintings
limitations: Painting domain only, one renderer, fixed payload and outcome-selected operating-point discussion. Nominal binomial FPR assumes fair independent null bits; 0/500 is not empirical proof of 1e-3. Borrowing VINE fidelity for other marks is a pilot-based assumption. The reported 27 seconds per 2048-canvas image on an unnamed consumer GPU is not our cost estimate. Probe decoder changed after clean failure and is exploratory.

title: Diffusion-Generated Image Watermarking: A Two-Axis Taxonomy and Three Protocol-Bounded Case Studies
limitations: Adjunct only: reused data dominate; no complete attack configuration or image denominator is supplied here. Table 2 harmonization and new HSTR quality do not make Tables 4/5 fresh experiments. The translated original is not counted again. A semantic carrier remains a hypothesis; editing conditions and native readouts differ across tables.

title: PECCVAI: Overcoming the Brittleness of AI Image Watermarking Under Visual Paraphrasing Attacks
limitations: Adjunct despite a genuine new benchmark: WDP combines bit accuracy and confidence across methods; maximum search needs image-level null calibration. No matched attack-quality operating points are established. Main embedding quality is not attack fidelity. The title spells PECCVAI and the body PECCAVI. Appendix human MOS was not read or borrowed.

title: Latent Watermarks under Generative Editing: A Benchmark and Analysis of Detection Survival
limitations: Conservative adjunct: ordinary editing rather than fixed regeneration/removal; seven of eight composite terms are added distortions. Native severity and semantic edits are not perceptually matched. Gaussian Shading/TAG limit d-prime analysis. Missing outputs are omitted. Code/artifacts are planned, not a verified release. This new study is distinct from the taxonomy, rather than independent confirmation of its reused tables.

title: Removal Attack and Defense on AI-generated Content Latent-based Watermarking
limitations: Same-pipeline inversion and optional original prompt differ from our independent, query-free regeneration; no empirical image-level FPR guarantee. The ideal-inversion/synthetic 15x claim is not a universal image gain. Printed Algorithm 4.2 uses budget 2|s|^2 <= epsilon although squared L2 cost of a sign flip is 4s^2; indexing also appears ambiguous. Preserve paper labels rather than silently implementing a correction. Appendix C figure labels say MSE while tables say RMSE. Table 4 rates .19/.01/.12 cannot all be two-decimal rounded binary counts out of the stated 30 images; repetitions or averaging are not explained, so no integer success counts are reconstructed.
